$schema_note: 12 NYCRR fee schedule provisions: Subpart 329-1 (Medical Fee Schedule) in full, and the sections carrying the 14 January 2026 proposed amendment (329-1.3, 329-4.2, 333.2, 343.2, 348.2) with their applicability siblings (329-4.1, 333.1, 343.1, 348.1). Clause text is the regulation's own text as compiled by LII and as restated by the Board in its own rulemaking documents; digests and the three-way agreement check are in source/PROVENANCE.md. $licensing_constraint: NO CLAUSE TEXT FROM ANY OFFICIAL NEW YORK WORKERS' COMPENSATION FEE SCHEDULE, AND NO CPT DESCRIPTOR, CODE TEXT OR TABLE. Both are licensed. Where the regulation itself quotes a fee schedule ground rule (329-1.3(e)(2)(v)) or a CPT descriptor (329-4.2(d), 333.2(c), 348.2(c)) the quotation is ELIDED and marked, and the code or rule is cited by identifier only. This is the demonstration: the register is evaluable, and a determination is verifiable, by a party holding zero clause text of the incorporated schedule.
$dispositions: MECHANICAL, JUDGMENT, CONDITIONAL, DERIVED, DEFINITIONAL, INSTRUCTION, ILLUSTRATIVE, and INCORPORATED_BY_REFERENCE. The last is new to the schema in this encoding: the operative rule is stated in a document the instrument incorporates by reference and which cannot be retrieved without purchase. It is a disposition with a distinct value, not undetermined and not unknown.
scope_note: IN: 329-1.1, 329-1.2, 329-1.3 (a) to (e); 329-4.1, 329-4.2; 333.1, 333.2; 343.1, 343.2; 348.1, 348.2. OUT, named rather than dropped: Subpart 329-2 (ambulatory surgery, APG methodology) and Subpart 329-3 (emergency room, hospital clinics) are fee schedule provisions but are not on the January 2026 amendment's path, and 329-2.1(b) carries CPT codes with descriptors and a dollar table in the regulation text itself, which the licensing non-goal excludes from reproduction. 12 NYCRR 325-1.8 (telemedicine), referenced by 329-4.2(d), 333.2(c) and 348.2(c), is public and retrievable and is outside scope; whether an encounter qualifies under it arrives as a supplied fact. WCL 13-g (arbitration committee) and Education Law 6738(a) are statute, not this instrument.

clauses.text: The fee schedule applicable to medical, physical therapy and occupational therapy services shall be the medical fee schedule in effect on the date on which the medical, physical therapy or occupational therapy services were rendered, regardless of the date of accident.
clauses.assertion: The governing edition is the one in effect on the date of service, not on the date of accident.
clauses.disposition_basis: Compares the edition a determination cites against the edition this register version holds as in effect, ordered against the date of service. For physical and occupational therapy services the applicability of THIS section, against 329-4.1(b), is open: ambiguity NY-A1.
clauses.$in_force_from_basis: renumbered from 329.1, State Register 2015-12-30; no later amendment listed by the compilation

clauses.text: When the schedule specifies a unit fee for a definite treatment and period of aftercare, and the patient is transferred from one to another physician, the employer (or carrier) is responsible for the amount stated in the schedule.
clauses.assertion: On transfer under a unit fee the employer owes the scheduled amount, once.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only where a unit fee is specified and a transfer occurred. The scheduled amount is licensed text; the determination supplies it as the applied bound and the register tests the total paid against it.

clauses.text: If the concerned physicians agree upon amount of proration, they shall render separate bills accordingly;
clauses.assertion: Agreed proration is billed separately.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only on an agreement.

clauses.text: in the event of no agreement, the matter shall be settled by by an arbitration committee appointed pursuant to section 13-g of the Workers' Compensation Law without cost to the contestants.
clauses.assertion: Disagreement is settled by a 13-g arbitration committee.
clauses.disposition_basis: Directs a referral. No fact of a bill makes it true or false. The doubled `by by` is the compilation's text and is kept.

clauses.text: When treatment is terminated by death before the expiration of the allowable period of aftercare, the appropriate fee shall apply without proration.
clauses.assertion: Death before aftercare ends leaves the full scheduled fee payable.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only on termination by death.

clauses.text: When treatment is terminated by departure of the injured worker from New York State before the expiration of the allowable period of aftercare, the fee shall be the earned portion of the appropriate fee, having regard for the fact that generally the greater portion is earned at the time of operation or other procedure.
clauses.assertion: On departure the fee is the earned portion.
clauses.disposition_basis: `earned portion` and `having regard for` name a standard and no test.

clauses.text: The medical fee schedule for medical services shall be the Official New York Workers' Compensation Medical Fee Schedule, updated December 11, 2019, prepared by the board and published by OptumInsight, which is herein incorporated by reference.
clauses.assertion: Identifies the edition of the medical fee schedule that is the fee schedule.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies the edition identity (update date, publisher) that the date-of-service clauses test a cited edition against. It decides nothing itself.
clauses.operative_weight: Edition identity: updated 2019-12-11, publisher OptumInsight, effective 2020-01-01 per State Register 2019-12-11.

clauses.text: [the fee amounts, relative value units, conversion factors and ground rules of the Official New York Workers' Compensation Medical Fee Schedule, incorporated by reference and not reproduced]
clauses.assertion: The operative fee rules are stated in the incorporated schedule.
clauses.disposition_basis: The rule a determination applies when it applies a scheduled amount is stated in a document this register does not hold and which 329-1.3(b) says may be purchased. Distinct from undetermined: the register knows where the rule is.

incorporated_document.document: Official New York Workers' Compensation Medical Fee Schedule
incorporated_document.retrieval: purchase, per 329-1.3(b); examination at the Department of State and listed libraries

clauses.text: The Official New York Workers' Compensation Medical Fee Schedule incorporated by reference herein may be examined at the office of the Department of State, One Commerce Plaza, 99 Washington Avenue, Albany, NY 12231, the Legislative Library, the libraries of the New York State Supreme Court, and the district offices of the board. Copies may be purchased from OptumInsight, by writing to Official New York Workers' Compensation Fee Schedule, PO Box 88050, Chicago, IL 60680-9920; by telephone at 1-800-464-3649, option 1; or online at www.optum360coding.com keyword New York or https://www.optum360coding.com/Product/40508/.
clauses.assertion: The incorporated schedule may be examined at listed public offices and purchased from the publisher.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies the retrieval condition the INCORPORATED_BY_REFERENCE clauses record: examination or purchase.
clauses.operative_weight: Retrieval condition of the incorporated document: examination at listed offices, or purchase from OptumInsight.

clauses.text: Physical Therapy Assistants (PTAs) and Occupational Therapy Assistants (OTAs) may provide services under the direct supervision of an authorized Physical Therapist (PT) or authorized Occupational Therapist (OT) respectively.
clauses.assertion: A PTA or OTA service is permitted only under direct supervision of an authorized PT or OT of the matching discipline.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only where the rendering provider is a PTA or OTA.

clauses.text: When billing for PTA services, supervising authorized PTs must select codes from the Physical Medicine Section of the Official New York State Workers' Compensation Medical Fee Schedule that are permissible and within the scope of practice for PTAs using modifier CQ.
clauses.assertion: PTA services are coded from a named schedule section.
clauses.disposition_basis: Which schedule the codes come from is recorded on the determination; the register compares it against the section this version names. THE NAMED SOURCE CHANGES BETWEEN VERSIONS: the Physical Medicine Section of the Medical Fee Schedule in force, the Acupuncture and PT/OT schedule under 329-4.2 as proposed.

clauses.text: [PTA services are billed] using modifier CQ.
clauses.assertion: A PTA service carries modifier CQ.
clauses.disposition_basis: Membership of a modifier in the bill's modifier list.

clauses.text: When billing for OTA services, supervising authorized OTs must select codes from the Physical Medicine Section of the Official New York State Workers' Compensation Medical Fee Schedule that are permissible and within the scope of practice of OTAs using modifier CO.
clauses.assertion: OTA services are coded from a named schedule section.
clauses.disposition_basis: As (c)(1), for OTAs. The named source changes between versions.

clauses.text: [OTA services are billed] using modifier CO.
clauses.assertion: An OTA service carries modifier CO.
clauses.disposition_basis: Membership of a modifier in the bill's modifier list.

clauses.text: Services billed using the modifiers CQ or CO must be billed and paid at 85 percent of the amount payable for such services had they been performed directly by PTs and OTs.
clauses.assertion: A CQ or CO service is paid at exactly 85 percent of the direct-therapist amount.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only where CQ or CO is billed. The direct-therapist amount is licensed schedule content and arrives as a supplied bound; the register tests the fraction. No rounding convention is stated: NY-A5.

clauses.text: Clinical notes by PTAs must be cosigned by the supervising PT. Clinical notes by OTAs must be cosigned by the supervising OT.
clauses.assertion: Assistant notes are cosigned by the supervising therapist of the same discipline.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only for a PTA or OTA service.

clauses.text: PTAs and OTAs may not provide services or bill for services independently.
clauses.assertion: The billing provider for a PTA or OTA service is never the assistant.
clauses.disposition_basis: Class of the billing provider against the assistant classes.

clauses.text: Nothing in this section shall change the maximum numbers of billable Relative Value Units (RVUs) for physical therapy and occupational therapy on any given date of service, as outlined elsewhere in the fee schedule. They are not increased or otherwise changed based on whether the services are provided by PTs, OTs, PTAs or OTAs.
clauses.assertion: The daily RVU maximum is the schedule's and is unchanged by assistant provision.
clauses.disposition_basis: The maximum itself is `outlined elsewhere in the fee schedule`, which is the incorporated document. The register records that the cap applies unchanged and does not hold its value. Under the proposed version `the fee schedule` for PTA/OTA codes is the Acupuncture and PT/OT schedule: NY-A6.

incorporated_document.document: the fee schedule incorporated by 329-1.3(a) (in force) or, for PTA/OTA codes, the schedule named by 329-1.3(c)(1) and (2) as proposed

clauses.text: When services are performed by PTs and PTAs (or OTs and OTAs) on the same date of service, the services applied to the maximum number of RVUs on any given date of service shall be determined giving priority to services provided by PTs over those provided by PTAs, and services provided by OTs over those provided by OTAs.
clauses.assertion: On a mixed day, therapist services are applied to the cap before assistant services.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only on a same-day mix. The determination records which class was given priority; the cap value itself is incorporated (c)(4).

clauses.text: The ability of PTAs and OTAs to provide services under NYS Workers Compensation, and for supervising PTs and OTs to submit bills for said services, shall in no way expand or otherwise change the scope of practice or permissible activities for PTAs or OTAs by statute, and/or any applicable regulations promulgated by the New York State Education Department, New York State Department of Health, or the New York State Workers' Compensation Board. As such, it shall be impermissible for PTAs/OTAs to perform any services or activities otherwise reserved for PTs and OTs respectively, or for supervising PTs or OTs to bill for such services, and Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes must be selected accordingly.
clauses.assertion: A service reserved to PTs or OTs by statute or regulation is impermissible for an assistant and may not be billed.
clauses.disposition_basis: Whether a service is `otherwise reserved` is decided by external statute and regulation the register does not hold; it arrives as a held assessment.

clauses.text: Examples may include, but are not limited to: a PTA is prohibited by section 6738(a) of the NYS Education Law from performing evaluation, testing, interpretation, planning or modification of patient/client programs; a PT conducts the initial evaluation and develops the plan of care, and the treatment may be provided by the PTA; PTAs and OTAs may not perform Functional Capacity Evaluations (FCEs).
clauses.assertion: Examples of reserved services.
clauses.disposition_basis: `Examples may include, but are not limited to`. It bounds (c)(6) by instance and tests nothing; the schema names ILLUSTRATIVE as not a category, and this clause is its second instance in the estate.

clauses.text: When workers' compensation benefits are sought due to a workplace exposure to COVID-19, reimbursement for serological, molecular or other reliable testing to confirm a current COVID-19 viral infection may be made using CPT code 87635.
clauses.assertion: Confirmatory COVID-19 testing on a workplace-exposure claim is billed under code 87635.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only where a test is billed on a workplace-exposure claim. The code is cited by identifier; its descriptor is not reproduced.
clauses.$in_force_from_basis: The compilation lists amendments effective 2020-03-16, 2021-04-07 and 2023-04-11 without attributing them to subdivisions; which one added (d) is not established here (NY-A4).

clauses.text: The RVU for CPT code 87635 shall be 39.18,
clauses.assertion: The relative value unit for 87635 is 39.18.
clauses.disposition_basis: A number stated in the regulation itself, so the register holds it and tests the determination's applied RVU against it.

clauses.text: and the total fee for such test shall be 51.33 for Region IV, 47.41 for Region III, and 41.53 for Regions I and II.
clauses.assertion: The fee for 87635 is fixed by region.
clauses.disposition_basis: Amounts stated in the regulation itself, selected by region. This is the one bound in the register that a party holding zero schedule text can verify to the cent.

clauses.text: CPT code 87635 may only be billed when there is a claim for workers' compensation due to a COVID-19 infection as a result of a workplace exposure or when testing for COVID-19 is administered as part of a required pre-operative testing protocol in accordance with Department of Health guidance.
clauses.assertion: 87635 is billable on exactly two bases.
clauses.disposition_basis: Membership of the recorded claim basis in a closed two-value set.

clauses.text: CPT code 87635 may not be billed for routine screening of workers' compensation claimants for the presence of the COVID-19 virus.
clauses.assertion: Routine screening is not a billable basis.
clauses.disposition_basis: The recorded basis against one prohibited value.

clauses.text: Antibody testing is not available under the Official New York Workers' Compensation Fee Schedule.
clauses.assertion: No antibody test is payable.
clauses.disposition_basis: A prohibited class against the tests billed.

clauses.text: CPT code 87635 may only be billed in one instance. Repeat testing is not permitted, except when clinical documentation supports a change or reoccurrence of symptoms, or a new exposure to the COVID-19 virus.
clauses.assertion: A repeat 87635 needs documented change, recurrence or new exposure.
clauses.disposition_basis: The exception arises only on a repeat.

clauses.text: Residents and fellows may provide services under the supervision of authorized physicians.
clauses.assertion: A resident or fellow service is permitted only under supervision of an authorized physician.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only where the rendering provider is a resident or fellow.
clauses.$in_force_from_basis: Notice of Adoption published State Register 2026-04-22; effective on publication per the Board's notice

clauses.text: The services provided must be in the context of an Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) accredited residency or fellowship program and cannot be part of any activities that are external to the program.
clauses.assertion: The service is within an ACGME-accredited program and not external to it.
clauses.disposition_basis: Two recorded booleans.

clauses.text: Residents and fellows may not provide services or bill for services independently,
clauses.assertion: The billing provider for a resident or fellow service is never the resident or fellow.
clauses.disposition_basis: Class of the billing provider.

clauses.text: and the supervising physician may not bill separately for the supervision of residents and/or fellows but rather, only for the specific clinical services performed.
clauses.assertion: Supervision is not separately billable.
clauses.disposition_basis: A recorded boolean on the bill.

clauses.text: When billing for non-surgical services provided by residents or fellows, supervising physicians must bill using the Official New York Workers' Compensation Medical Fee Schedule
clauses.assertion: Non-surgical resident services are billed under the medical fee schedule.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only for a non-surgical resident or fellow service.

clauses.text: and use the modifier 1R.
clauses.assertion: A non-surgical resident service carries modifier 1R.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only for a non-surgical resident or fellow service.

clauses.text: Services billed using the modifier 1R must be billed and paid at the same amount payable for such services had they been performed directly by the supervising, authorized, billing physician.
clauses.assertion: A 1R service is paid at exactly the direct-physician amount.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only where 1R is billed. The direct amount is licensed schedule content and arrives as a supplied bound.

clauses.text: When billing for services performed by a resident or fellow functioning as an assistant at surgery, supervising physicians must bill using the Official New York Workers' Compensation Medical Fee Schedule
clauses.assertion: Resident assistant-at-surgery services are billed under the medical fee schedule.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only for a resident or fellow assisting at surgery.

clauses.text: and use the modifier 84.
clauses.assertion: A resident assistant-at-surgery service carries modifier 84.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only for a resident or fellow assisting at surgery.

clauses.text: Codes billed with modifier 84 must accurately represent work performed by the resident or fellow and be documented appropriately in the surgical report.
clauses.assertion: An 84 code accurately represents documented resident work.
clauses.disposition_basis: `accurately represent` and `documented appropriately` name standards and no test.

clauses.text: Resident/fellow surgical services billed using modifier 84 must be billed and paid at 16% of the physician code fee or fees, and only for the procedure or procedures in which the resident or fellow assisted.
clauses.assertion: An 84 service is paid at exactly 16 percent of the physician fee.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only where 84 is billed. The physician fee is licensed schedule content and arrives as a supplied bound. No rounding convention is stated: NY-A5.

clauses.text: If different resident(s) or fellow(s) provide assistance on different procedures or portions of procedures, then the supervising surgeon may bill for the surgical assistant services for each such procedure or portion of a procedure, but only for one such assistant for each procedure or portion of a procedure.
clauses.assertion: At most one resident assistant is billed per procedure or portion.
clauses.disposition_basis: A count of distinct resident assistants billed for the procedure under determination. Emitted before (i), which reads it: (i) is the exception layer over this count.

clauses.text: The supervising surgeon may bill for no more than one resident or fellow (even if more than one resident or fellow assisted) for any procedure or portion of a procedure for which the resident(s) or fellow(s) provided assistance, unless the length, complexity or number of the procedure(s) require multiple resident(s) or fellow(s) to assist, in which case the use of more than one resident or fellow as assistants must be clearly documented contemporaneously at the time of the procedure and in the medical narrative at the time of billing.
clauses.assertion: More than one resident assistant is billable only where complexity requires it and that is contemporaneously documented.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only where more than one resident is billed (reads (ii)). Whether complexity `require[s]` multiple assistants is a held judgment; the documentation is a recorded fact.

clauses.text: If other physicians, physician assistants or nurse practitioners are also utilized as assistants at surgery in conjunction with residents or fellows, the supervising surgeon may bill for no more than one assistant, unless the length, complexity or number of the procedure(s) require multiple assistants, in which case the use of more than one assistant must be clearly documented contemporaneously at the time of the procedure and in the medical narrative at the time of billing.
clauses.assertion: With mixed assistant classes, more than one assistant in total is billable only where complexity requires it and that is documented.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only where other-class assistants are billed alongside a resident. STATED LIMIT: the list of all assistants billed and the list of resident assistants are supplied separately and their consistency is not checked.

clauses.text: Surgical services billed for resident and/or fellow surgical assistants using modifier 84 must be billed on the same bill as the underlying surgery.
clauses.assertion: An 84 line is on the surgery's bill.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only where 84 is billed.

clauses.text: For non-surgical services using modifier 1R, a single bill reflecting the services and/or level of service provided to the patient on any given day or at any given appointment must be submitted, and supervising physicians cannot submit two separate bills for resident and/or fellow services and supervising physician services on the same date of service, unless the bills are for demonstrably different services, and designating services as "resident and/or fellow services" versus "supervising physician services" shall not be considered demonstrably different services.
clauses.assertion: A 1R day is one bill unless the bills are for demonstrably different services, and the resident/supervisor designation alone is not a difference.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only where 1R is billed and more than one bill exists for the day. `demonstrably different` is a held judgment whose one excluded ground is stated.

clauses.text: Nothing about this subdivision shall change the rules or application thereof related to the billing for "Co-Surgeons" or "Assistant Surgeons" or "Minimum Assistant Surgeons" or "Surgical Teams", nor shall it apply to inpatient hospital billing, as these terms are outlined and addressed elsewhere in the Official New York Workers' Compensation Medical Fee Schedules, and not specifically pertaining to residents and fellows,
clauses.assertion: Co-surgeon, assistant-surgeon, surgical-team and inpatient rules are the schedule's and are unchanged.
clauses.disposition_basis: The rules are `outlined and addressed elsewhere in the Official ... Medical Fee Schedules`: the incorporated document.

incorporated_document.document: Official New York Workers' Compensation Medical Fee Schedule, surgery ground rules on co-surgeons, assistant surgeons, minimum assistant surgeons, surgical teams, and inpatient hospital billing

clauses.text: except that this subdivision shall supersede the provision in Surgery Ground Rule 12(B) of the Official New York Workers' Compensation Medical Fee Schedule that states [one sentence of Ground Rule 12(B), quoted in the regulation, ELIDED here under the licensing constraint].
clauses.assertion: Subdivision (e) displaces the one Ground Rule 12(B) sentence barring assistants' fees where the hospital supplies resident staff.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies a meaning the 16 percent clause consumes: the schedule's own bar on resident assistant fees does not apply to an (e)(2) payment. The displaced sentence is identified by rule number; its text is not reproduced.
clauses.operative_weight: Surgery Ground Rule 12(B), one sentence, superseded for resident and fellow assistants at surgery.

clauses.text: Medical narratives, clinical notes, procedure notes, and/or operative reports must clearly state the name of the resident or fellow, as well as the name of the supervising physician, and the program or institution where the services are being performed.
clauses.assertion: The narrative names the resident, the supervising physician and the program.
clauses.disposition_basis: Presence of three recorded fields.

clauses.text: The ability of residents and fellows to provide services under NYS Workers' Compensation, and for supervising physicians to submit bills for said services, shall in no way expand or otherwise change the scope of practice or permissible activities for residents and fellows by statute, and/or any applicable regulations promulgated by the New York State Education Department, New York State Department of Health, or the New York State Workers' Compensation Board.
clauses.assertion: Subdivision (e) does not enlarge scope of practice.
clauses.disposition_basis: Bounds the grant in the chapeau rather than testing a fact; unlike (c)(6) it states no operative prohibition of its own.
clauses.operative_weight: Scope of practice for residents and fellows is the external statute's and regulations', unchanged.

clauses.text: The fee schedule applicable to acupuncture services shall be the acupuncture fee schedule in effect on the date on which the acupuncture services were rendered, regardless of the date of accident.
clauses.assertion: The governing acupuncture edition is the one in effect on the date of service.
clauses.disposition_basis: As 329-1.1, for the acupuncture schedule.

clauses.text: The fee schedule applicable to physical therapy and occupational therapy services shall be the physical therapy and occupational therapy fee schedule in effect on the date on which the physical therapy or occupational therapy services were rendered, regardless of the date of accident.
clauses.assertion: The governing PT/OT edition is the one in effect on the date of service.
clauses.disposition_basis: As 329-1.1, for the PT/OT schedule. 329-1.1 says PT and OT services use the MEDICAL fee schedule; this says the PT/OT schedule. Both are in force. Which governs is NY-A1 and is not settled here.

clauses.text: The acupuncture fee schedule for acupuncture services shall be the Official New York Workers' Compensation Acupuncture and Physical Therapy and Occupational Therapy Fee Schedule, created December 11, 2019 prepared by the Board and published by OptumInsight, which is herein incorporated by reference.
clauses.assertion: Identifies the edition of the acupuncture schedule.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies the edition identity the acupuncture date-of-service clause tests against.
clauses.operative_weight: Edition identity: created 2019-12-11, publisher OptumInsight, effective 2020-01-01.

clauses.text: [the acupuncture fee amounts, units and ground rules of the incorporated schedule, not reproduced]
clauses.assertion: The operative acupuncture fee rules are stated in the incorporated schedule.
clauses.disposition_basis: As 329-1.3(a)/incorporation.

clauses.assertion: Identifies the edition of the PT/OT schedule.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies the edition identity the PT/OT date-of-service clause tests against. clauses.text: Authorized acupuncturists, physical therapists, and occupational therapists shall use Common Procedural Technology (CPT) code 99441 [descriptor quoted in the regulation, ELIDED under the licensing constraint] when telemedicine is used in accordance with section 325-1.8 of this Title, notwithstanding this code not appearing in the Official New York Workers' Compensation Acupuncture and Physical Therapy and Occupational Therapy Fee Schedule.

incorporated_document.document: Official New York Workers' Compensation Behavioral Health Fee Schedule

clauses.text: The Official New York Workers' Compensation Behavioral Health Fee Schedule incorporated by reference herein may be examined at the office of the Department of State, One Commerce Plaza, 99 Washington Avenue, Albany, NY 12231, the Legislative Library, the libraries of the New York State Supreme Court, and the district offices of the board. Copies may be purchased from OptumInsight, by writing to Official New York Workers' Compensation Fee Schedule, PO Box 88050, Chicago, IL 60680-9920; by telephone at 1-800-464-3641, option 1; or online at www.optum36-coding.com keyword New York or https://www.optum360coding.com/Product/40508/.
clauses.assertion: The incorporated schedule may be examined at listed public offices and purchased from the publisher.
clauses.disposition_basis: Retrieval condition. The compilation's `1-800-464-3641` and `www.optum36-coding.com` differ from the Board's restatement (`1-800-464-3649`, `www.optum360coding.com`); kept as compiled, recorded under NY-A3.
clauses.operative_weight: Retrieval condition: examination at listed offices, or purchase from OptumInsight.

clauses.text: Authorized providers, including psychologists and licensed clinical social workers, shall use the following Common Procedural Technology (CPT) codes when telemedicine is used in accordance with section 325-1.8 of this Title, notwithstanding these codes not appearing in the Official New York Workers' Compensation Behavioral Health Fee Schedule. [...] (1) 99441 [descriptor ELIDED]; (2) 99442 [descriptor ELIDED]; and (3) 99443 [descriptor ELIDED].
clauses.assertion: A qualifying telemedicine encounter by these providers is coded 99441, 99442 or 99443.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only where telemedicine under 325-1.8 is used.
clauses.$in_force_from_basis: compilation lists an amendment effective 2023-04-11 without attributing it to a subdivision

clauses.text: Use of these codes are limited to one unit per patient per day.
clauses.assertion: At most one unit of the telemedicine codes per patient per day.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only where one of the three codes is billed.

clauses.text: Use of these codes are not eligible for the enhanced reimbursement in Modifier 1B of Ground Rule 9.
clauses.assertion: The telemedicine codes never carry the 1B enhancement.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only where one of the three codes is billed. Modifier 1B and Ground Rule 9 are the incorporated schedule's; the register tests only that 1B is absent from the bill.

clauses.text: The fee schedule applicable to podiatry services shall be the podiatry fee schedule in effect on the date on which the podiatry services were rendered, regardless of the date of accident.
clauses.assertion: The governing podiatry edition is the one in effect on the date of service.
clauses.disposition_basis: As 329-1.1, for the podiatry schedule.
clauses.$in_force_from_basis: the compilation lists no amendment history for 343.1

clauses.text: The podiatry fee schedule for podiatry services shall be the Official New York Workers' Compensation Podiatry Fee Schedule, updated December 26, 2018, prepared by the board and published by OptumInsight, which is herein incorporated by reference.
clauses.assertion: Identifies the edition of the podiatry schedule.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies the edition identity the podiatry date-of-service clause tests against. Note the edition date differs from the other four schedules.
clauses.operative_weight: Edition identity: updated 2018-12-26, publisher OptumInsight, effective 2019-04-01 per State Register 2018-12-26.

clauses.text: [the podiatry fee amounts and ground rules of the incorporated schedule, not reproduced]
clauses.assertion: The operative podiatry fee rules are stated in the incorporated schedule.
clauses.disposition_basis: As 329-1.3(a)/incorporation.
